title: Current WebSocket baseline
summary: The current Git source candidate is ooRexx WebSocket Access v0.1-dev4; v0.1-dev1 remains the immutable qualified release. dev4 adds server-side RFC 6455 access, coalesced-handshake byte preservation and a parsed owned-HTTPS upgrade handoff while retaining SocketProvider/TLS authority boundaries.
invariants: Qualified delivery remains oorexx_websocket_access_v0.1-dev1.zip with SHA-256 91d244cb00216f5760bffe2e2983c1e461d89048e8fd668f4ad160636eb0a655.
Git source candidate v0.1-dev4 includes dev2 fragmentation/close repairs, dev3 estate crypto adapter, and dev4 server/HTTPS handoff.
Client and server handshakes preserve already-read WebSocket bytes beyond the HTTP header terminator.
WebSocketServerAccess accepts a plaintext duplex stream already owned by the socket/HTTPS layer; it does not acquire TCP or TLS itself.
WebSocketUpgradeRequest and acceptParsedRequest() form the explicit parsed-request handoff for the owned ooRexx HTTPS server.
Current external Socket Provider authority remains v0.1-dev16 with SHA-256 fe2fa086bd4f1e072b8d455e6adb4475482b8db6a35118329f6b3f6e6253c8c2.
Current optional crypto authority remains ooRexx Crypto v0.8.3 SHA-256 5ebcab81493287499719f98920cb190d37afc79992cb34c7772d5392f63b9b49 plus crypto.auth/0.1.
Stable packages/oorexx_https_server API inspected 2026-10-29 documents v0.4.6 and intentionally hides raw transport objects from ordinary route/interceptor handlers.
Do not rewrite dev1 history to claim a fresh dev16 or owned-HTTPS qualification.
Rasen Falcon coordination lane is websocket-access.
